# TypeScript Linter Specialist Skill

**Category:** Tech Skills > Frontend > TypeScript

## Purpose

Provides specialized knowledge, step-by-step procedures, and quality standards for TypeScript Linter Specialist operations using TypeScript technology. This skill encapsulates technology-specific best practices, design patterns, performance optimization techniques, and production-grade implementation guidance for TypeScript within Frontend development.

## When to Use

- When configuring ESLint for TypeScript projects
- When creating custom ESLint rules for project conventions
- When migrating from TSLint to ESLint with typescript-eslint
- When TypeScript-specific technical expertise is required
- When best practices for TypeScript technology stack must be applied
- When production-grade TypeScript implementation guidance is needed

## Capabilities

- Configure eslint with typescript-eslint parser and plugin
- Set up type-aware linting rules
- Create custom ESLint rules for project conventions
- Configure flat config for modern ESLint setup
- Integrate linting with CI/CD pipeline

## Procedure

1. Assess project linting requirements
2. Configure ESLint with typescript-eslint
3. Select appropriate rule presets
4. Add custom rules for project conventions
5. Configure IDE integration for real-time linting
6. Set up CI/CD linting step

## Technology Standards

| Standard / Best Practice | Relevance |
|--------------------------|-----------|
| **typescript-eslint** | Official TypeScript ESLint parser and rules |
| **Flat Config** | Modern ESLint flat configuration format |
| **Type-Aware Rules** | Rules that use TypeScript type information |

## Anti-Hallucination Rules

- Do not use deprecated TSLint configuration
- Verify eslint and typescript-eslint version compatibility
- Do not fabricate version numbers, API endpoints, or library names
- Always cite the specific documentation, RFC, or standard being referenced
- If technology-specific data is unavailable, explicitly state the gap and request clarification
- Never assume features exist in a specific version without verification

## Quality Checks

- Rules catch common TypeScript anti-patterns
- Type-aware rules do not slow linting significantly
- Configuration is consistent across team
- All code examples must be syntactically valid and tested
- Cross-reference findings against official documentation
- Flag any assumptions made during analysis with explicit markers
- Validate all performance claims with reproducible benchmarks
- Ensure all recommendations follow TypeScript community best practices
